publications.title: The Berlin Pride terrorist Attack: How Europe remains vulnerable
publications.venue: CISES - Centre for International Security and Economic Strategy
publications.summary: What does Berlin's Pride terrorist attack reveal about European security gaps? During Berlin’s Christopher Street Day celebrations, a car drove into the crowd near the Brandenburg Gate, killing one person and injuring dozens. The attacker, a 21-year-old German citizen who claimed responsibility on behalf of ISIS, fits the profile of the homegrown lone actor that European security agencies struggle most to detect. The attack underscores how public festivals, open streets, and minority communities remain exposed despite years of strengthened counter-terrorism measures.

publications.venue: CISES (Center for International Security and Economic Strategy)
publications.summary: This video explores : 1) The significance of Suu Kyi's first know contact with an international representative since 2021. 2) Why the junta released the images now. 3) The political context surrounding Myanmar's April 2026 elections. 4) The junta's efforts to improve its relationship with ASEAN. 5) How the images could help Myanmar's military project legitimacy and reduce international pressure..
